images.filename: Battle of White Sulphur Springs Plan.png
images.caption: A Union Army brigade commanded by Brigadier General William W. Averell planned a raid with multiple objectives. It was unable to accomplish its third objective because it was stopped by a Confederate force command by George S. Patton in the Battle of White Sulphur Springs.
images.alt: A Union Army brigade commanded by Brigadier General William W. Averell planned a raid with multiple objectives. It was unable to accomplish its third objective because it was stopped by a Confederate force command by George S. Patton in the Battle of White Sulphur Springs.

images.filename: Prelude to Battle of White Sulphur Springs.png
images.caption: This map shows the first few days of Br. Gen. William W. Averell's first West Virginia Raid that led to the Battle of White Sulphur Springs in August 1863 during the American Civil War.
images.alt: This map shows the first few days of Br. Gen. William W. Averell's first West Virginia Raid that led to the Battle of White Sulphur Springs in August 1863 during the American Civil War.

images.caption: This map shows the two days of movements by Br. Gen. William W. Averell's before Battle of White Sulphur Springs in August 1863 during the American Civil War.
images.alt: This map shows the two days of movements by Br. Gen. William W. Averell's before Battle of White Sulphur Springs in August 1863 during the American Civil War.

images.filename: Battle of White Sulphur Springs Union Map.png
images.caption: The map is from Plate CXXXV-B, No. 3, from the Atlas to Accompany the Official Records of the Union and Confederate Armies. It shows the Battle of White Sulphur Springs, which occurred on August 26-27, 1863, in the American Civil War. The Union brigade commanded by Br. Gen. William W. Averell was stopped by a Confederate force commanded by Col. George Patton.
images.alt: The map is from Plate CXXXV-B, No. 3, from the Atlas to Accompany the Official Records of the Union and Confederate Armies. It shows the Battle of White Sulphur Springs, which occurred on August 26-27, 1863, in the American Civil War. The Union brigade commanded by Br. Gen. William W. Averell was stopped by a Confederate force commanded by Col. George Patton.
images.artist: Published under the direction of the U.S. Secretaries of War by Major George B. Davis (U.S. Army), Leslie J. Perry (civilian expert), and Joseph W. Kirkley (civilian expert). The map itself was drawn by Lieutenant John R. Meigs, who was present at the battle. The map has been enhanced and identifiers added by TwoScarsUp.

images.caption: After the Battle of White Sulphur Springs on August 26-27, 1863, a Union brigade commanded by Brigadier General William W. Averell retreated and evaded pursuing Confederate cavalries.
images.alt: After the Battle of White Sulphur Springs on August 26-27, 1863, a Union brigade commanded by Brigadier General William W. Averell retreated and evaded pursuing Confederate cavalries.

images.filename: Beginning Battle of White Sulphur Springs.png
images.caption: Troop positions at the beginning of the Battle of White Sulphur Springs in the American Civil War on August 26, 1863. Scaling based on map drawn by Lieutenant John R. Meigs. Troop location based on book "The Battle of White Sulphur Springs" by Eric J. Wittenberg.
images.alt: Troop positions at the beginning of the Battle of White Sulphur Springs in the American Civil War on August 26, 1863. Scaling based on map drawn by Lieutenant John R. Meigs. Troop location based on book "The Battle of White Sulphur Springs" by Eric J. Wittenberg.

images.filename: Battle of White Sulphur Springs Confederate Map.png
images.caption: This map shows the Battle of White Sulphur Springs as drawn by the Confederate Army. The battle occurred on August 26-27, 1863, during the American Civil War.
images.alt: This map shows the Battle of White Sulphur Springs as drawn by the Confederate Army. The battle occurred on August 26-27, 1863, during the American Civil War.
images.artist: The publication's editor is Lt. Col. Robert N. Scott. The original map was drawn by someone reporting to Colonel George S. Patton of the Confederate Army. The map has been enhanced and identifiers added by TwoScarsUp.
